name: IA-04
label: Likely R

key_factors: Open seat after Feenstra retired to run for governor
Prediction markets price Republicans at about 94%
Democrat Dawson badly outraised by Republican McGowan
model.rationale: The seat's R+15 lean and the absence of any Democratic polling or outside spending point to a Republican hold, and markets agree at roughly 94% Republican. The open seat and modest Democratic fundraising add some uncertainty, but nothing suggests a competitive race.
model.watch: A polarizing Republican nominee or a late surge of Democratic outside spending could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Randy Feenstra (R) is not on the ballot.

overview: Randy Feenstra's retirement to run for governor leaves this heavily Republican northwest Iowa seat open. The district's R+15 partisan lean gives the Republican nominee a large structural advantage, and Chris McGowan has raised far more money than Democrat David Dawson, with no outside spending on the Democratic side. Prediction markets price the Republican at about 94% to win. No expert raters have flagged the race and no public polls are available, so the forecast rests mainly on fundamentals. The expected margin is a Republican win of roughly fourteen points, with elevated uncertainty because it is an open seat with no polling to anchor the estimate.
